text:
Alex: quick sketch — thinking about adding a tiny predictor that assigns per-prefix TTLs (or a hotness score) so eviction decisions are based on predicted next-hit time rather than raw recency
Maya: interesting. is this RL or supervised?
Alex: MVP = supervised regressor that predicts next-hit delta (ms). longer term we can reward for fewer miss-regen cycles (rl/bandit) but want simple first
Tony: how do you see this fitting with the current lease/lease-epoch flow? don't want TTL fights vs lease ownership
Alex: TTL would be advisory to the eviction scorer only. leases still control ownership/handshake. if a prefix has an active lease we ignore eviction TTLs
Sara: metrics we should track: eviction-induced miss rate, cold-start p99, token cost delta, and per-tenant regressions. also need data retention/privacy checks
Maya: model features idea: recent hit count, inter-arrival mean/std, last 5 intervals, prefix size, tenant tier, time-of-day bucket, upstream latency trend. absolutely hash prefix key before storing
Jules: can we expose feature importance in the console? product wants to explain when a tenant sees more evicts
Alex: yes — plan is to emit SHAP-lite scores sampled at 0.1% for explainability. default is aggregated importance metrics per-model per-tenant in console
Tony: inference cost? if this runs on every eviction decision it'll add CPU at scale. need batching or async scoring
Maya: run model as a tiny quantized ONNX on the node, cache predictions for X seconds, and async-refresh. or host a local gRPC predictor with hot cache of recent prefixes
Alex: config sketch (yaml):
```
rl_ttl:
  model: prefix_tiny_v1
  mode: shadow   # shadow / enabled / off
  sample_rate: 0.05
  min_ttl_ms: 100
  max_ttl_ms: 3600000
  cache_ttl_ms: 1000
```
Tony: rollout proposal: shadow mode for 2 weeks on 5% of prefixes, compare shadow TTLs vs baseline heuristic and collect: shadow_miss_delta, tail_latency_change, cpu-infer-cost
Sara: must ensure we log no raw user text. store only hashed prefix id + numeric features + timestamps. GDPR: retention 30 days by default for training data unless opt-in
Maya: training cadence? weekly retrain should be fine. we can use reservoir sampling across tenants to avoid bias to big customers. consider upweighting enterprise tier during training to avoid harming SLAs
Jules: product asks for safety constraints: never increase eviction aggressiveness for premium tenants; cap TTL reduction to 20% for tier=A
Alex: fallback: if model fails or confidence low, revert to current heuristic. also expose a per-tenant opt-out flag
InfraBot: deploy check: model binary < 300KB compressed, inference p95 < 0.5ms per prediction when cached; alert if model qps > 5000 and node cpu>70%
Tony: A/B metrics: aim for -15% regen cost and p99 <= 0 change. if we see p99 regression > 5% rollback automatically
Maya: one more: collect false positive/negative signatures — when model predicted long TTL but we saw regen within window. useful for tuning loss and reward shaping
Alex: action items:
- Maya: prototype predictor + minimal feature extractor (2 days)
- Tony: integration shim to feed advisory TTL into eviction scorer (3 days)
- Sara: spec for logging/retention + privacy review (1d)
- Jules: product acceptance criteria + dashboard fields (1d)
We'll run 5% shadow for 2 weeks, then canary 1% enabled with automatic rollback thresholds
Tony: sounds good. ping me when prototype emits first predictions
Maya: will do. I'll post a short notebook and sample metrics
Alex: thanks all, sending follow-up RFC doc + perf checklist later today :thumbsup:
